# MakeUp/BSL existing volumetric-budget concept transfer

Two maintained adapters now have genuine native consumers for the unchanged Sildur/Bliss uniform_sample_budget concept, alongside existing SSR refinement. Existing CoreABI2/owned REFINEMENT_ADAPTER flag is reused; no new uniforms, shared helper edits, renderer/research route or generic shader rewrite was added. Family helpers include the existing shared function once inside their original uniform/include guard, avoiding duplicate declarations. Packaged mirrors match source; parent owns catalog/digest integration and builds/runtime.

MakeUp9.5g targets its Overworld deferred sky cloud get_cloud loop, native CLOUD_STEPS_AVG10/V_CLOUDS1. Count is changed before the original increment=(upperPlane-lowerPlane)/samples and increment_dist; native full physical slab, per-step opacity length, first-contact density logic, sampler calls, native AA/lighting and final cloud normalization stay in place. Existing policy/min4 yields Balanced9 and Performance8. Deferred sky only, not water reflections, End/Nether/unknown/DH/VOXY. This is approximate sample-count LOD, distinct from the closed exact saturation/explicit-LOD cloud trial; no break, sampler or threshold rescue occurs. PBR/cloud reflection callers are untouched; material compatibility remains unverified.

BSL10.1.8 targets the deferred1 sky Aurora24 call only. DrawAurora itself retains native sampleStep=1/samples, full unit interval, per-step attenuation and radiance weighting; existing policy/min4 yields Balanced21 and Performance18. The12-sample sky-reflection caller stays native. DH/VOXY/ADVANCED_MATERIALS fall back to24. Native384 has AURORA0, so this optional feature is inactive in the reference/default scene: no default-scene work or FPS benefit is claimed. Native32/64 cloud marching was intentionally not adapted because its per-step absorption, cloudLighting/distanceFade and cloudViewLength feedback need a different algorithm; native7 exponential shafts also remain unchanged rather than truncating their integration domain or retuning policy.

Actual pinned original archives assemble through build_supported_pack_adapters.apply/build. Native member drift and wrong shared-helper SHA refuse for both, unchanged upstream members and original bytes are preserved, helper uniforms deduplicate. Generated source digests are recorded in dev/logs/bsl-makeup-volumetric-budget-port-20261011/assembly-and-boundary-checks.json for parent integration; new source/member/helper SHA pins and mirrors are current. Original licenses/member attribution remain intact; generated ZIPs are ignored local evidence only.

Helper-leaf GLSL330 compatibility syntax checks pass. The initial strict GLSL120 sanity check fails an existing unchanged refinement helper integer max/min overload; raw log is retained. No native-stage GLSL120 pass, Iris transform or driver compilation is inferred from the330 leaf checks. Native consumer preprocessing/driver compatibility, actual linked controls/avoided samples, still/motion/AA quality, PBR/DH and original-relative speed remain unverified. No client, loader build, benchmark or owned job was launched. Source is frozen for parent integration; CPU released.

## D16 value boundary and R4 negative finding

D16 unsigned-normalized storage cannot contain NaN/Inf/subnormal floating
members. Its positive normalized rational minimum is 1/65535, well above
`Float.MIN_NORMAL`; zero is deliberately allowed in the finite domain and
conservatively blocks the positive-minimum shortcut. This is a readback-independent
domain inference from the normalized conversion and D16 storage contract.
Steady admission is limited to actual D16/16/UNSIGNED_NORMALIZED; D24/D32/D32F
and unknown formats remain native. [OpenGL 4.1 §§2.1.2, 2.11.11,
Table 3.13](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/glspec41.core.pdf).

The required value proof is about shader X(t): identical raw integer fetches
must produce the same converted value, the producer min must select an existing
operand, and R32F must preserve that normal/zero float through store and fetch.
It never requires X(t) to equal the CPU readback conversion. Min selection and
float storage preserve the proposed mathematical argument only after the actual
linked producer/terrain paths are reviewed and root qualifies the same-GPU value
path. [GLSL 3.30 §§4.1.4, 8.3](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/GLSLangSpec.3.30.pdf).
No admission row was populated here; no file/config bit or passing sparse
finite scene can stand in for this review.

Root reported mature R4 at armed frame 10241: stamp −10242 correct, 10,735
distinct D16 depth readback values, and 15 of 16,383 useful GPU minima one ULP
above CPU `glGetTexImage(D16→GL_FLOAT)` minima. Example: CPU
0.5019607543945312, GPU field 0.501960813999176. Receiver qualification stayed 0.
Those parent-recorded observations were not independently measured by this
worker. The worker read root's [all-15 counterexample receipt](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r1/bsl-raw-runtime-r4/parent-cpu-gpu-path-counterexample.json)
and [actual source/resource inventory](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r1/bsl-raw-runtime-r4/parent-source-resource-inventory.json).
The producer pair is `727c7a5a0e099cb431476a256d4e5e6627a818ff00a5e754f5a9a45a25a004a0`;
terrain candidate pairs are `efede257944d5c65b04c87e33feaef6f22bd7527a664bf03b5a30c3a50720c50`
and `2d35051b73f245bd37535bb07d3e8d14968d35db8b724d4b9714a71194ee170b`.
These are provenance, not populated admission rows. R3's sparse 78-value frame remains its limited earlier exact result;
R4 is preserved as a negative CPU-conversion/equality result. **No tolerance,
equality gate or R4 classification was changed.** Root's proposed raw-fetch→R32F
GPU echo and complete consuming-source audit remain necessary next evidence.

Root also observed field MIN/MAG LINEAR. For the new steady explicit level-zero
`texelFetch`, filter weights are unused. Steady therefore accepts only NEAREST

all identity/format/state checks remain. The old finite observer retains its

continuation, native hardware fallback and default private options are preserved.
Original-native archive remains the absolute quality/cost denominator. Main-mod

## Native work and changed allocation

Primary entry is `surface/parallax.glsl:6–38`; terrain caller is `gbuffers_terrain.glsl:169–180`. Original native work reads the normal sentinel, rejects invalid tangent view input or fully faded relief, samples initial height, then performs up to128 explicit-gradient height samples with first-crossing termination. Native fade is unchanged:64–96 radial world blocks at DISTANCE64. It has no mip/footprint primary-count exit. Hand, water, entity and block-entity callers keep their original signatures/counts.

For native height in `[0,1]`, primary displacement lies on the complete local tile-UV segment

`R = viewVector.xy / -viewVector.z * PARALLAX_DEPTH * (1 - nativeFade)`.

The candidate changes step size and loop count together: `1/N`, `R/N`, at most N advances over the same complete `[0,1]` height domain. It does not truncate a 128-step ray after 40 native-size steps. The existing normal sentinel, height samples, first-crossing equations, wrapping, material consumers and complete `GetParallaxShadow` function are preserved. Reduced sampling can nevertheless select a different first height intersection and change UV/surfaceDepth and downstream appearance.

For certified constant orthonormal tangent basis `T,B,N`, reconstruct view position `V = T*viewVector.x + B*viewVector.y + N*viewVector.z`. Let clip position `C=P*(V,1)`, U displacement `A=P*(T*R.x,0)`, V displacement `D=P*(B*R.y,0)`. Physical tile spans along either basis axis lie in `[0,1]`. Define `wmin=C.w-|A.w|-|D.w|`; reject unless `wmin>.75*C.w>0`. Ideal-real projection gives the conservative per-axis pixel derivative bound

`M = .5*viewport*(|A.xy*C.w-C.xy*A.w| + |D.xy*C.w-C.xy*D.w|) / wmin²`.

For any height interval of length 1/N, projected movement is at most M/N per axis under that contract. This covers independent U/V spans≤1 and perspective over the whole ray, rather than inverting a local UV derivative and calling it a finite bound. The shader adds a 10% arithmetic allowance; formal binary32/driver error certification is **unverified**. Native jitter translates projected XY and cancels algebraically from the numerator, so AA-off remains eligible without enabling/replacing AA.

Count is at least32, at least `ceil(1.1*max(M)/.125 output pixel)`, and at least `ceil(max(abs(R)*tileTexels)/.25 base-level texel)`, capped at the selected native quality. These are spacing limits per axis, not a bound on normal/emission/lighting error or narrow-height intersection identity. Unknown HDR radiance is not used to invent an energy bound.

Full native work protects core Off/Quality/missing ABI, unsupported pack/version/format, DH/VOXY/curvature, invalid dimensions/view/basis, non-opaque category, invalid tile sizes, native quality<64, grazing tangent cosine≤.35, ray wrapping or proximity within one base-level texel of a tile border. Near count is full through DISTANCE/4; smoothstep blends the request until DISTANCE/2, followed by ceiling to an integer. Native distance fade/cutoff remains exactly selected. This continuous request reduces abrupt count changes but does not prove absence of temporal popping. A modeled5-pixel full-ray slope gives counts128/115/84/54/40 at16/20/24/28/32blocks.

The classifier runs before expensive primary traversal, with no extra texture, mip, target, history or resolve. # BSL native128 POM maximum-height interval proof R1

**Conditional source proof and one UNWIRED consumer; defer runtime.** A maximum over every actual native height sample in a future interval can prove that interval contains no first hit. The existing evidence does not provide that maximum, complete mip contents, a native address error bound, or a current producer/query/binding contract. No candidate ZIP, integration, cue, quality admission or performance claim follows.

Worker `/root/bsl_height_interval_proof` owns only this report and [ignored evidence](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r3/bsl-height-interval-proof-r1/). Parent owns source/build/checkpoints and the client/GPU lane. No worker-owned live processes; CPU released after this bounded proof. Closed previous-cell cache, projected-UV count/step and cloud policies remain closed unchanged. This is a distinct producer/consumer architecture, not tuning of those candidates.

## Pinned source and evidence

BSL10.1.8 by Capt Tatsu, https://capttatsu.com, original archive SHA-256 `36b0a50ff7918bf10e9422c401d93779f9d0088a26acea975b435243f96930b5`, was rehashed and five relevant members extracted without modifying original bytes. Replete1.2.0 SHA-256 `6a967ac89bd1f05c42c0d0fa2f606b5b894b3b52bcc624c72c48b33a1d48a2c6` and the retained original observation SHA-256 `27a5e1e0e7cda310cf733fac78a71719973282f4801561c153ad54789e32d5a7` reproduce. Member hashes are in [proof-receipt.json](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r3/bsl-height-interval-proof-r1/proof-receipt.json); attribution remains in the prototype, and no distribution/license change is proposed.

Entry points are `shaders/world0/gbuffers_terrain.fsh/.vsh` → `shaders/program/gbuffers_terrain.glsl` → `shaders/lib/surface/parallax.glsl`, `ReadNormal` and `GetParallaxCoord`. `ReadNormal` uses `fract(coord)*vTexCoordAM.pq+vTexCoordAM.st`, then `texture2DGradARB(normals,coord,dcdx,dcdy)`. Terrain defines `dcdx=dFdx(texCoord)` and `dcdy=dFdy(texCoord)` before material/march branches; the consumer retains these inputs and introduces no derivatives. Primary POM samples alpha; initial RGB normal rejection, downstream albedo/material sampling and `GetParallaxShadow` remain native.

The retained actual image is2048×1024RGBA8, native MIN9986/NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR, MAG9728/NEAREST, base0/max4, REPEAT, with recorded anisotropy1, bias0 and LOD clamps0..4. Levels1..4 dimensions, completeness and contents were not established by the base-only observation. Old object IDs/upload epoch cannot authorize a new consumer. The prior embedded-source hash encoding qualification remains unchanged; this work does not newly join a driver source to a current texture. See [all-mip reuse R2](bsl-pom-mip-support-reuse-r2.md).

[Corrected original PBR budget R2](../evaluation/bsl-original-pbr-gpu-budget-r2.md) measures opaque/cutout3.74348ms and separately sampled frame9.61821ms, whole scopes only. It does **not** attribute3.74348ms to POM or establish interval coverage. No new runtime observation was made.

## Certificate and preservation proof

Define native state at sample index `j` by the actual repeated operations `p[j+1]=F32(p[j]+stepDir)` and `c[j+1]=F32(c[j]-1/128)`, starting at native `p[0]` and `c[0]=1`. This notation is the binary32 oracle model; the GPU's compiled arithmetic requires separate verification. Let `h[j]` be the native returned alpha with the actual packed-atlas mapping, original gradients, image and sampler. Native tests `c[j] <= h[j]` at indices0..127, advances to128 only if no earlier hit, and returns the resulting UV/currentStep.

For a proposed skipped interval `J={a,...,b}`, require a finite upper bound `U` with `h[j] <= U` for **every** `j in J`, and `U < min(c[j]:j in J)`. Therefore every omitted hit test is false. Strict `<` is required: equality is a native hit. Native128 depth steps decrease, so the endpoint is the minimum; the prototype computes that endpoint with repeated subtraction rather than substituting a formula.

Inductively, each certified state has the same coordinate and depth as native, and native cannot terminate there. The first uncertified state reads native alpha and executes the native test. Thus first-hit index, returned UV and surfaceDepth match, conditional on a valid supplier and matching compiled recurrence. The final cap sample128 is deliberately left native; no terminal special case or depth substitution is needed. Unchanged self-shadow receives the same inputs and uses its unchanged native samples. This is a logical preservation proof, not a driver pixel-equality result.

An actual native mip pair may blend two nearest alpha samples. A maximum over the complete support of **all eligible actual mip levels0..4** bounds any such pair without selecting or guessing LOD, provided conversion/interpolation rounding is conservatively covered. This observation does not rely on driver derivatives being reconstructed. General normalized filtering and finite-precision qualifications are in [OpenGL4.1 sections2.1.1,3.8.11–3.8.12](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/glspec41.core.pdf); GLSL numeric limitations are in [GLSL3.30 section4.1.4](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/GLSLangSpec.3.30.pdf). No accepted numeric/address error budget is available here.

## Producer/query/update contract still missing

The producer must derive upward-rounded **maximum alpha bounds from each actual mip image**, with storage/image/upload epochs and dimensions/format/completeness checked. Native average-filter mip content cannot be replaced by a synthetic max-mip texture used for native sampling. A separate maximum hierarchy may summarize existing actual mip images, including their coarse levels. Base-cell maxima only become sufficient if a separate proved relationship bounds every actual eligible mip; no such relationship is assumed.

The query must conservatively enclose all *actual repeated-add positions*, then their actual post-fract atlas support, REPEAT behavior and native nearest-address uncertainty at every eligible level. Local wrapping requires splitting support across both sprite edges; a clamped local interval or endpoint-only rectangle may miss it. No shader-side `floor(uv*size)` classification, guessed margin or straight affine endpoint jump is admitted without its numeric support bound. Conservative supersets may include adjacent atlas tiles; they may reduce useful skips, but cannot discard potential samples to improve coverage. Native `fract`/mapping remain unchanged; no new tile clamp is inserted. Nonfinite/grazing coordinates or unproved support fall back. Bounding the entire image avoids spatial classification but usually returns a high maximum; useful coverage is unknown.

Upload, subimage, reload, animation, atlas rebuild/reallocation and sampler changes invalidate affected bounds before use. A producer must bind to the actual active `normals` image and draw/source contract, not a named Replete asset, authored sprite or old GL ID. Native/consumer memory visibility and publication must be synchronized; invalid or unavailable data uses native reads until current bounds are established. Real texture access, update hooks, binding and publication are dependencies of the parent's separate API investigation, not implementations supplied here.

## Exactly one unwired consumer

[consumer-unwired.glsl](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r3/bsl-height-interval-proof-r1/consumer-unwired.glsl) declares `TryNativePOMHeightIntervalBoundUnwired` with no implementation and no caller. It accepts a proposed span and maximum only under the supplier contract, verifies span limits and the strict endpoint comparison, omits height fetches before they execute, and retains every native UV/depth operation. It stores only remaining certified count and whether the current height is certified; it never tests a stale alpha after an interval. If the next certificate fails, it reads the next native height before testing it. The prototype is not linked, parsed, loaded or packaged; undefined supplier is intentional. There is no invented TRUE uniform, observer, Java helper or framework.

`allowIntervals=false` performs no supplier queries and retains native fetch/test behavior; unsupported quality retains the native loop. Future controls would have to admit only actual bridge2/enabled1/preset0..2, with Off, Quality, missing preset−1, absent/invalid provider and unsupported state native. Those controls are not connected here. Native fade64–96 radial world blocks and its32-block transition remain unchanged. UV is normalized sprite/atlas coordinate; depth/currentStep is normalized height, not world distance. No distance threshold or transition is added by this exact certificate.

## Counterexamples and checks actually run

[check_proof.py](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r3/bsl-height-interval-proof-r1/check_proof.py) ran successfully with192 small deterministic binary32 arbitrary-height oracle cases: equality first hits at each index0..127,32 cap cases and32 arbitrary height cases. Native and consumer coordinate/depth traces agree, and all192 disabled runs retain native fetch count with zero queries. The oracle enumerates future heights to manufacture valid bounds; **that is not a usable provider or sampling model**, and its fetch counts are not predicted runtime coverage or physical texture transactions.

Five asserted counterexamples are preserved: base height0.1/coarse height1 with mip weight0.75 returns0.775 and can hit depth0.7 despite a base-only certificate; height0.9 below current depth1 still hits later depth0.875; equality0.75 is a hit;32 repeated binary32 additions differ from a multiplied endpoint; local wrap0.999→1.001 moves selected32-wide atlas support from base cell351 to320. These are synthetic logical examples, not observed driver defects. Native source/sampler assertions and archive/member hashes also passed.

No GLSL compiler/parser, project build/tests, client/reload, fresh GL query, actual provider construction, native sampling validation, cue, still/motion quality, compatibility or GPU timing ran. Static proof does not establish compiled bitwise recurrence parity under GLSL compiler optimization.

## Cost and decisive boundary

Charge initial producer work reading2,793,472 texels across the ideal complete2048×1024 levels0..4, plus maximum reduction, upward rounding, allocation/storage, actual image discovery/validation and synchronization. A dense F32 scalar copy of those mip alphas alone is10.66MiB before hierarchy nodes; a hierarchy adds storage/reduction work. This is a sizing example, not a chosen implementation or measured cost. Every relevant update must regenerate or invalidate affected summaries; per-frame update amortization cannot be assumed away.

Charge per-ray/per-interval guards, repeated-add support construction, atlas fract/wrap splitting, native address uncertainty expansion, hierarchy queries at all eligible levels, scalar endpoint recurrence, comparisons/branches, registers and fallback queries. The consumer retains all original UV/depth ALU and adds up to one extra depth subtraction per proposed interval sample; a failed query also pays its prefix. A provider that enumerates/readbacks all native samples at each query has already spent the work it proposes to save. Shader divergence, register pressure and compiler/native texture-cache reuse remain unknown. There is no positive cost case or eligible-ray coverage admission from source lookup counts.

**Stop here:** conditional mathematics is proved; actual conservative supplier and current resource support are not. If a complete provider later becomes available, parent must first establish compiled/source/current-resource consumption and native-preserving controls, then ordinary still/motion quality. Needed cost evidence is matched original/fullwork-control/consumer/original-return total-frame and opaque/cutout GPU timings with native128, sampler, resource, options, scene, warmup and resolution matched; include producer/update/query/ALU/binding overhead and use function-level physical evidence only if available. The existing whole-terrain budget does not promise a POM saving. No gain, quality/cue admission or project-completion claim is made.

# BSL active AO work pilot R1

2026-10-07, owner `bsl_real_budget`. Isolated source pilot only; production adapters,
registries, Java and ports unchanged. Mac runtime is owned by `mac_performance_owner`.
No client, GPU capture, Windows SSH, commit or background process was started here.

## Why this path

The shipped BSL adapter trims only distant water SSR refinement. It cannot explain
useful gains over ordinary inland terrain and does nothing with DH. This pilot
instead changes the screen-wide ambient-occlusion pass, which is enabled in BSL's
native HIGH/default profile. This is an explicitly pinned adaptation of a reusable
lower-resolution effect producer plus depth-aware reconstruction mechanism; it
can be implemented in other packs without rewriting their scene render graphs.

BSL 10.1.8 has native TAA, not a proven native TAA upscaling path. Scene-wide raster
scaling is deferred because the necessary producer/consumer, jitter, depth,
reprojection/history and translucent contracts are absent. It would be unsafe to
infer them from the presence of TAA alone. This is one AO resolution experiment,
not a sequence of shader quality/sample-count reductions.

## Pin and reproduction

Original `dev/upstream/other-pack-research/BSL_v10.1.8.zip`, SHA256
`36b0a50ff7918bf10e9422c401d93779f9d0088a26acea975b435243f96930b5`.
Upstream credit: BSL Shaders v10 Series by Capt Tatsu, https://capttatsu.com.
Publisher license is All Rights Reserved; personal local experimentation only,
no redistribution grant or publication. Original ZIP is never modified; all 309
original members and attribution remain in the generated copies. Four upstream
members change, two private helpers are added, 305 upstream members are exact.

Maintained isolated recipe and builder:
`patches/experiments/bsl-real-budget-r1/manifest.json`, `build.py`,
`reconstruct.glsl`, `validate.py`. The kernel is generated from the pinned original
`ambientOcclusion.glsl`, with only depth samples changed to explicit LOD0. The
recipe pins the source and complete resulting helper hash; no upstream shader
kernel source is copied into tracked files.

```sh
python3 patches/experiments/bsl-real-budget-r1/build.py --arm disabled --output build/BSL-AO-half-disabled-r1c.zip

```

## Producer, consumer and boundaries

Private option `SHADERLOD_BSL_AO_HALF_RES=0` defaults off; 1 enables the pilot.
No core mod uniform or automatic preset connection is implemented. A future
managed integration must reload the matching compile option; Quality and Off
must choose 0/original. Uniform enable flags cannot resize an already compiled
viewport and are not used to pretend such a connection exists.

- `world0/deferred.fsh` -> `program/deferred.glsl` retains the native 4 directions,
  2 depth samples per direction, reconstructed normal, radius and native TAA noise
  evolution. The enabled producer outputs AO plus positive camera-space linear
  depth to private `colortex10`, `RG32F`, `RENDERTARGETS:10`.
- `scale.world0/deferred=0.5` renders only the lower-left half of each axis of a
  full-resolution private buffer. Expected native 1920 x 1200 target is paired
  with 960 x 600 AO viewport: one quarter of AO producer fragments, not one
  quarter of total rendering cost. The texture itself is full sized. This adds
  two private full-size ping-pong allocations and reconstruction fetches.
- `world0/deferred1.fsh` -> `program/deferred1.glsl` keeps its native full-resolution
  scene/cloud/reflection outputs. Four nearest private AO/depth texels are fetched
  at explicit LOD0, with bilinear spatial and continuous depth-confidence weights.
  Its sampler is `colortex10`, GLSL `sampler2D`, consuming `.rg`.
- AO native radius remains 0.25 camera-space blocks. Depth tolerance is
  `max(0.25 blocks, 0.01 * positive linear depth)`. Confidence fades smoothly as
  neighbor depth differences cross 0.25 to 1.0 of that tolerance. No distance
  tiers or camera-motion sample dithering are added.
- Depth-discontinuous pixels execute at most ONE complete current-pixel native AO
  kernel, then blend by confidence. Smooth pixels execute zero fallback kernels.
  All fallback depth/noise reads use explicit LOD0, so the branch does not require
  unverified implicit derivatives. Edge filtering differs from native four-tap
  filtering of a full-resolution AO buffer; silhouette/still/motion quality must
  be inspected. Quarter producer + full resolve + occasional full kernel does
  not imply quarter AO cost, still less quarter total-frame cost.
- Existing `colortex4`/`gaux1` is left at native resolution and retains its later
  cloud-distance role. It is not resized, nor used to hide incompatible depth
  packing. Scene resolution, geometry, shadows, native reflection loop counts,
  cloud sampling, full-resolution TAA/history and jitter are unchanged.
- Initial enabled scope is **Overworld, native AO enabled, DH and Voxy absent**.
  The affected shaders explicitly reject other enabled cases. Native options,
  alternative AO methods, AA off, DH/domain reconstruction, dimension changes,
  odd resolutions and resizing remain runtime-unverified; this is not broad
  compatibility or production support.

Viewport/flip behavior is consistent with the [Iris rendering contract](https://shaders.properties/current/reference/shadersproperties/rendering/):
viewport scaling changes the rendered portion, not texture allocation, and deferred
passes write alternate buffers then flip. Runtime must prove the actual pinned
Iris interpretation; the documentation alone does not prove the produced frame.

## Checks actually run and needed evidence

`glslangValidator` checked 12 flattened shaders: original/disabled/enabled x
`deferred`/`deferred1` x vertex/fragment. All passed. Offline compiler inputs use
GLSL 330 compatibility with explicit MC_VERSION 12101 and IS_IRIS;
this matches the intended language features, not Iris's real patched source or

`dev/logs/bsl-real-budget-r1/glsl-check.json` and adjacent `.frag`/`.vert` files.
The first include expander failed on a relative include; that tool error was
corrected without modifying the shader candidate, then the complete check passed.

All four disabled affected shaders preprocess/token-normalize exactly equal to
the original (`disabled-parity.json`). The disabled branch uses upstream helpers,
outputs, AO filtering and full viewport; private work is compiled out. Original
ZIP/member immutability and generated scope were checked by the builder.

No runtime or performance claim. Client owner needs original -> candidate ->
original, native loaded option equality apart from the private switch, source/
Program join, actual producer viewport/draw framebuffer RG32F attachment and
consumer texture identity/dimensions, then matched GPU timing and total frame/FPS.
Resource/viewport observation proves the work-area contract, not an executed
invocation counter. Quality needs foliage silhouettes, contact shadows, camera
motion, steep depth changes, hand geometry, sky boundaries and several viewpoints.
A reduction in AO fragments may be outweighed by private-buffer bandwidth,
reconstruction, fallback and unaffected passes; no +20% promise follows.

## Cost review correction before runtime

Root relayed the independent Astra concern: the initial r1 fallback evaluated

## Actual Iris format parsing correction R1c

The parallel Complementary real Apple shader compile rejected its newly added
format tokens outside comments. BSL's r1b `const int colortex10Format = RG32F;`
was likewise outside a comment, with no GLSL definition. Our offline validator
had incorrectly injected an enum definition and therefore masked this problem.
No BSL runtime attempt occurred; the same defect was predicted from exact source.

Stock BSL `program/final.glsl` encloses its `const int ...Format` directives in
multiline comments. Actual pinned Iris 1.8.12 `ConstDirectiveParser.findDirectives`
bytecode splits lines and parses the const token without stripping comments;
`PackRenderTargetDirectives` consumes its string through InternalTextureFormat.
A direct JShell invocation against the actual shipped Iris JAR returned
`[ConstDirective { INT colortex10Format = RG32F; }]` for the multiline-comment form.
Exact bytecode and invocation output are retained in
`const-directive-parser-bytecode.txt`, `render-target-parser-bytecode.txt`, and
`actual-iris-comment-parser.txt` under the same ignored evidence directory.

R1c uses the native comment form, preserving RT10/RG32F allocation and every
sampling/work-area/fallback contract. The synthetic RG32F definition was removed
from the offline validator; all twelve shaders and four disabled parity checks
passed again. MC_VERSION/IS_IRIS preamble values remain explicit intended Iris
compile context, and language version330compat remains an offline translation
qualification; neither proves driver linking. Native raw wrappers are GLSL120.

## One bounded LOD candidate after the original smoke

The most direct default-workload candidate is **water parallax only**, with the
original native `WATER_PARALLAX=false` option as the lower-quality control.

`program/gbuffers_water.glsl::GetWaterHeightMap` L133 samples two noise layers
for default `WATER_NORMALS=1`. `GetParallaxWaves` L158–165 performs four height
evaluations: eight source noise fetches. `GetWaterNormal` L175–176 uses that
displaced position, then L184–187 performs four more height evaluations for its
normal: another eight fetches. Native parallax-off skips the first eight while
keeping the latter normal construction. Actual driver instructions/cache costs
and whole-frame savings remain unmeasured.

A future default-off explicit experiment could retain those four displacement
iterations near water, use fewer literal iterations in a medium band, and skip
displacement far away while retaining the original normal/lighting/SSR path.
Use reconstructed `length(viewPos)` in camera-space block units; the existing
varying `dist` is vertex-derived/interpolated and also used inside the native
displacement formula. Preserve that formula rather than silently replacing all
distance uses. Avoid changing `WATER_NORMALS`, turbulence or reflected clouds
in the same experiment.

A continuous transition can attenuate displacement in the near/medium band;
it saves the skipped evaluations only in the fully cheap region. Blending two
fully evaluated normals costs both kernels. Existing animated noise plus TAA
does not prove a newly dithered budget will be stable. Inspect grazing views,
reflection edges, wave shimmer, motion and the far-band boundary. Changing
parallax position changes normals and therefore reflection geometry; this is a
quality tradeoff even though lighting budgets remain untouched.

New nonuniform branches around `texture2D(noisetex, ...)` require a derivative
review. Prefer verified explicit LOD/gradient sampling on the active path, with
gradients prepared before divergence when needed. The wrappers already enable
ARB texture LOD, but actual driver translation and noise texture mip/filter
state still need verification. Preserve a complete original path when disabled.

Do not first cut `lib/reflections/raytrace.glsl`'s 30-iteration outer budget:
its collision-driven contraction/growth and `maxf` refinements affect reach and
hit precision. Full water reflections already use `maxf=4` when normals are on.
POM already has a native distance fade and is inactive in the default material
profile. Those are less useful first targets than isolating existing water work.

worker proposes no adapter implementation or publication.

## Exact arithmetic scope and fallback

Only two expressions inside the fixed native `Raytrace` loop are specialized:
forward `gbufferProjection * vec4(viewPos, 1)` followed by XYZ/W, and native
`gbufferProjectionInverse * vec4(ndc, 1)` followed by XYZ/W. Matrices use GLSL
column indexing. Accepted centered perspective rows are
`[a,0,0,0]; [0,b,0,0]; [0,0,e,f]; [0,0,-1,0]`; accepted inverse rows are
`[A,0,0,0]; [0,B,0,0]; [0,0,0,D]; [0,0,C,E]`.
The forward helper uses `(a*x,b*y,e*z+f)/(-z)`, and inverse uses
`(A*nx,B*ny,D)/(C*nz+E)`. It retains the original XYZ/W division and subsequent
forward `*0.5+0.5` order; it does not substitute reciprocals or reassociate the
nonzero two-term expressions.

Exact zero/shape, finite coefficient and coefficient magnitude <= 1e10 checks
run once per ray, only after core control admits the experiment. Both matrices
must match; there is no assumption from matrix naming. Off-axis/asymmetric or
jittered matrix offsets, orthographic matrices, nonfinite coefficients, missing
shape entries, or excessive coefficients select the original expressions.
Initial start/viewPos/vector magnitudes must each be <= 1e6, and call parameters
must satisfy 0 <= inc <= 2 and 0 <= ref <= 1. The fixed <= 30-step native recurrence
then bounds positions to below about 2.2e15; finite scalar products are below
about 2.2e25. A per-step |viewPos.z| > 1e-10 guard keeps specialized forward outputs
below about 2.2e35, inside binary32 finite range. The inverse requires that this
same sample used the specialized forward path, depth in [0,1], and |inverseW| >
1e-10; clipped forward XY then bounds finite inverse outputs below about 2e20.
A failed forward guard also forces native inverse for that sample, preserving
native NaN propagation at singular projection inputs. Matrix/inverse consistency
is not assumed or needed to specialize either independently shaped expression.

This removes explicit zero matrix terms: roughly 16 multiplies/12 additions per
full transform become 3 multiplies/1 addition forward and 3 multiplies/1 addition
inverse, before divisions. These are source expression counts, not driver
instruction or savings evidence. Uniform shape and finite guards, ray checks,
and per-sample denominator/depth branches are added costs. The compiler may
already exploit native sparsity, and the candidate may cost more. No work is
hidden after depth sampling: forward selection occurs before the depth sample;
inverse selection occurs before its matrix work. Native rays, maximum 30 steps,
step/refine parameters, depth sample coordinates/counts, bias, error threshold,
dist metric, hit termination, reprojection, and rough color gather remain native.
No new sampling, derivative dependency, distance band, or quality threshold is
introduced. Distances remain native view-space/world-block units. The fast path
has no distance transition; enable/preset changes follow existing shader reload
behavior, and arithmetic rounding still requires still/motion checks.

Floating-point equivalence is not a claim of bit-identical native GLSL execution.
Zero-term removal may affect signed zero, and driver multiply-add contraction,
dot lowering and reassociation can differ. Singular denominators use native code.
The Python scalar model uses explicit binary32 separate multiply/add rounding;
it is evidence about that model only.

## Arithmetic, transitions and native fallback

Native terrain declares `dcdx=dFdx(texCoord)`/`dcdy=dFdy(texCoord)` before `main` divergence. ReadNormal maps `fract(coord)*vTexCoordAM.pq+vTexCoordAM.st` and uses those fixed textureGrad inputs. Native vertex construction maps the local0..1 tile corners to those atlas coordinates. Therefore J=[dcdx dcdy] describes atlas UV change per raster pixel; the native complete relief ray is `R=viewVector.xy*PARALLAX_DEPTH/-viewVector.z*(1-nativeFade)` in local tile UV. This candidate forms atlasRay=R*vTexCoordAM.pq and solves:

```
det = dcdx.x*dcdy.y - dcdy.x*dcdx.y
screen.x = (dcdy.y*atlasRay.x-dcdy.x*atlasRay.y)/det
screen.y = (dcdx.x*atlasRay.y-dcdx.y*atlasRay.x)/det
N = clamp(ceil(2*max(abs(screen.x),abs(screen.y))),8,128)
sampleStep=1/N; stepDir=scaledDir*sampleStep*(1-nativeFade)
```

`AtlasPBRLoader.load(TextureAtlas,ResourceManager,PBRTextureConsumer)` owns PBR sprite construction, CPU mip generation and native atlas upload. It obtains base width/height/mip count via Iris `TextureAtlasAccessor`, calls `PBRSpriteContents.increaseMipLevel`, then `PBRAtlasTexture.tryUpload(width,height,mipLevel)`. `PBRAtlasTexture.upload(III)` calls `TextureUtil.prepareImage`, fills **every level 0..mipLevel** with native default color, uploads sprite first/current frames, and installs the object in the base PBR holder. `PBRSpriteContents.getMipmapGenerator()` selects current texture-format custom generator or linear fallback. A base-level-only maximum therefore cannot stand in for the generated native mip images.

`PBRAtlasTexture` width/height/mipLevel are protected; no public getters expose them. On the render thread, temporarily bind the observed native texture and call `glGetTexLevelParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, level, WIDTH/HEIGHT/INTERNAL_FORMAT/ALPHA_SIZE)` for each allowed level, plus current base/max, sampler and swizzle state. A pinned cap 0..4 yields five actual image checks; a general bounded inspection caps at the GL maximum texture-size-derived chain length. `TextureInfoCache` does not provide an all-mip/content-generation certificate. Read each native mip directly in producer GLSL with `texelFetch(sourceNormals, ivec2, nativeMip)`; no CPU image readback is required for production. Completeness/format/coordinate/support admission must precede permission.

## Content-change boundary, including animation

Existing `BslPrefixAtlasR8Mixin` fences `upload(III)V`, `uploadSprite(PBRTextureAtlasSprite)V`, `clear()V`, `close()V` at HEAD. Existing texture/resource/manager/format/pipeline hooks fence release/filter/reload/delete/destroy and identity changes. These can invalidate storage and static content. Existing R8 rejects animated selected sprites and takes one finite readback, then retires rather than refreshing. It is not a full-atlas dynamic producer.

**Missing fence:** `PBRAtlasTexture.cycleAnimationFrames()V` binds the PBR atlas and directly iterates `TextureAtlasSprite.Ticker.tickAndUpload()`. It bypasses `uploadSprite`. `MixinTextureAtlas` injects at `TextureAtlas.cycleAnimationFrames()V` TAIL; `PBRAtlasHolder.cycleAnimationFrames()` invokes normal and specular PBR animation. Object IDs and all existing storage/resource fences can remain unchanged while normals/mips change. No public content-generation counter or update event exists in the inspected classes.

One exact bounded fix is a NORMAL-only HEAD/RETURN fence on `PBRAtlasTexture.cycleAnimationFrames()V`: revoke permission at HEAD, mark dirty after RETURN. Conservatively mark every cycle dirty, even if no actual frame advances; do not claim exact upload counts. This covers native ticker interpolation without tracing every NativeImage upload. An exceptional/incomplete call must stay invalid. Initial upload, uploadSprite, close, release and resource/format transitions still need their existing fences. Arbitrary third-party GL writes are outside this certificate and must disable the route unless explicitly covered. An unchanged-hook alternative rebuilds the entire source hierarchy on every consuming frame/draw, but still needs an ordering and no-intervening-upload assumption and pays full repeated cost; it does not certify content epochs.

Run bounded GLSL 330 raster producer over the **actual native mip images** into mod-owned scratch targets, then max-reduce according to the separately admitted interval representation. A straightforward version constructs a hierarchy per native mip, retaining its own extents. Reduction uses disjoint input/output texture objects; copy completed scratch images into the final hierarchy store. This seam is available in bytecode but **is not currently installed by existing BSL mixins**. Default supplier returns a complete conservative fallback. GL 4.1 / GLSL 330 supports integer-coordinate mip `texelFetch` and renderable R32F targets. Separate scratch objects avoid undefined texture/FBO feedback; same-object different-mip reduction is not assumed safe. See [GL 4.1](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/glspec41.core.pdf), sections 3.8/4.4.3, and [GLSL 330](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/GLSLangSpec.3.30.pdf), texture functions. ## State, budget and control safeguards

A producer must preserve GL current program, VAO/array buffer, draw/read FBO, draw/read buffers, viewport/scissor, active unit and every changed texture target/sampler binding; preserve depth test/mask, blend and indexed blend/color masks, cull, polygon/rasterizer-discard state and any changed sRGB state. Use matching RenderSystem/Iris state APIs or restore both driver and cached state; raw restoring only GL values can desynchronize Minecraft caches. Pixel pack/unpack/PBO state matters if transfers are added. Native `FullScreenQuadRenderer.begin/end` disables then **unconditionally enables** depth testing; it is not by itself an arbitrary-state save/restore scope. Existing BslFieldCullScope saves only culling, insufficient for this producer. Avoid `Program.use()` paths that disturb Iris active uniform/sampler listeners unless those listener states are restored; a private raw producer with complete state scope is bounded but requires source implementation and validation.

Source generation markers are invalidation signals, not byte hashes or proof of values. Atomically publish a generation only after all required levels finish and recheck identity/epoch. Never expose a partially rebuilt hierarchy or reuse a prior generation after animation. If a fixed update-work cap is exceeded, abandon/revoke for that epoch and run native POM; amortization cannot expose stale bounds. Off must bypass both new producer and shader skip; a fullwork control should pay the same producer/binding/query overhead while retaining native march, then candidate enables interval skips. Current main UI/core readbacks alone cannot certify this path.

Cost unknowns are decisive: complete 0..4 source images total 2,793,472 texels at historical extents; full per-mip pyramids add reduction outputs and multiple raster/copy dispatches. Full rebuild on a native animation tick can repay that cost repeatedly, even for a tiny animated sprite. There is no measured producer cost, skip coverage, allocation budget, content-update frequency or original-relative benefit. Partial dirty rectangles require another precise affected-parent update design; not an assumed cheap optimization. No long benchmark is warranted before admission.

## Exact quad and same-frame construction

[Pinned FullScreenQuadRenderer bytecode](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mip-parity-source/FullScreenQuadRenderer.javap.txt)
shows `renderQuad()` calls only polygon-mode override, the existing quad's draw,
and polygon-mode restoration. `begin()` saves/binds its VAO and disables depth;
`end()` restores its saved binding and enables depth. The replay therefore calls
**renderQuad only**, from the original c7 RETURN, before Iris restores blend
state or advances to final. It never reenters begin/end. The paired native
HEAD/RETURN must have the same actual program, VAO, pipeline, frame, uniform
values, input identities and output identities.

At the real draw boundary, require a complete nondefault FBO, the full fixed
viewport, fill polygon mode, no active program pipeline/transform feedback/query,
no depth/stencil/scissor/raster discard/logic operation, single-sample storage,
disabled blend on both outputs and all color channels writable. Draw buffers
must map only locations0/1 to attachments0/1. Each attachment must be an ordinary
2D level0 texture with the exact format and extent. Native RT1/RT2 read and write
images are joined through RenderTargets and the pass's stageReadsFromAlt.

Every active input texture must be distinct from **both** native output textures.
This is essential: the completed original draw must not have changed an input
that the replay would read. A current/history ping-pong pair is checked for both
RT1 and RT2; depth is also included in the nonalias check. All samplers must be0,
with native wrap, base0, max level1000, LOD −1000…1000, bias0 and anisotropy1.
RT1 starts mip-linear/linear, RT2 linear/linear and depth nearest/nearest.

The primitive then:

1. Reads complete native current RGB8 and history RGBA16 output storage.
2. Allocates two private textures of those same formats and extents, initialized
   to the exact bytewise complement of the corresponding native output. It
   reads them back and verifies that initialization before drawing.
3. Attaches only those private textures to a private MRT framebuffer, retaining
   native viewport, program, VAO, uniforms and all input bindings. It changes
   only the actual RT1 input texture's MIN_FILTER from9987 to9729 and verifies
   every input binding and that intended filter difference before replay.
4. Replays the exact native quad once, reads both scratch outputs, records full
   native/replay hashes and mismatch byte/texel counts, and reads native outputs
   again to verify they were left intact.

The inverse initialization makes an undrawn/unwritten texel differ from native
in every stored byte. It therefore prevents an all-zero/uninitialized scratch
target or missing draw from accidentally passing a dark early-frame comparison.
Each readback independently fills two CPU buffers with different poison bytes,
performs both complete reads and requires identical results. Unwritten bytes
cannot pass by retaining the same default allocation contents. The class does
not consume GL error flags or claim that getters are independently error-free.
The paired reads and verified inverse initialization provide direct failure
detection for no/partial data transfer or draw writes in this primitive.

Readbacks use RGB/UNSIGNED_BYTE for RGB8 and RGBA/UNSIGNED_SHORT for RGBA16.
These fixed normalized storage formats contain finite quantized values; the
comparison is exact over all returned stored component bytes, without tolerance
or NaN normalization. Pixel pack/unpack buffers must be0 and all queried
row/image/skip/swap/LSB state canonical, alignment4. The fixed widths give tightly
packed rows for both formats. Temporary CPU storage peaks at approximately
80.6 MB; it and both scratch textures/FBO are released in the same callback.

## Poison, full reads and scratch write coverage

Each output contains 2,304,000 texels: RGB8 requires 6,912,000 bytes and RGBA16
requires 18,432,000 bytes. Pack/unpack PBOs must be 0; alignment is 4, row/image
lengths and skips are 0, swap and LSB flags are false. Row sizes are therefore
5,760 and 15,360 bytes, with no hidden row padding. `glGetTexImage` uses the
bound texture and format/type conversion, and a bound pack PBO would reinterpret
the pointer as an offset; these are the relevant [Khronos readback rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Refpages/main/gl4/glGetTexImage.xml).

Lines 454–465 initialize two full CPU buffers to distinct bytes `0x35`/`0xca`,
read the same image twice, and require equality. A byte left untouched in both
reads must differ, so a failed/no-write read cannot masquerade as an all-zero
result. Under the specified GL transfer semantics, equality supplies a complete
result vector; it is not a universal certificate against arbitrary faulty-driver
data. Absolute buffer puts and LWJGL calls leave position/limit at the full
allocation, so ByteBuffer equality and hashing cover the complete byte range.

Lines 474–496 initialize every private component to the bytewise complement
of native output, then verify the upload by full readback. Complementing both
bytes of each unsigned 16-bit component is also its exact integer complement;
no fixed value equals its complement. A texel or component left unwritten by
replay therefore cannot equal the native output. The exact scratch internal
formats and full extents are checked before attachment, and the MRT must be
complete. This makes a missing draw, partial color mask, discard or incomplete
coverage fail the comparison instead of accidentally passing on initial zeros.
It does not identify the cause of a mismatch: private storage/FBO substitution
is also a change, so a mismatch is not automatically caused by minification.

Only the RT1 input MIN_FILTER changes before replay, from 9987 to 9729. Actual
sampler bindings/filters and uniform bits are rechecked, all output bytes are
compared, and both original native images are read again for immutability.
Matching normalized RGB8/RGBA16 readback is an exact comparison of returned
stored components; it is not a floating-point tolerance or NaN normalization.

Let X(t) denote the resulting shader float from a current raw depth texel.
The producer chooses each cell minimum from all 256 X values. If the field's
stored/fetched value is that same selected float, every X in the cell is >= m.
Every fetched query operand lies in a queried cell. Thus four m >= reference

pre-average primary sum equals 9. Candidate misses execute the same specified
raw reference query on the stored footprint. This proves the **algorithm within

base-relative explicit LOD, and undefined out-of-range/incomplete accesses.

selects an operand. §4.5.1 supplies no arithmetic error bound.

R11 and R13 actual steady witness JSONs were checked directly: each has three samples at arm +1/+61/+121, 122 normal producer returns, and both terrain programs at each sample report actual linked `shaderlodBslRawQueryQualified = 1`, matching frame/shadow/render epochs, matching live owner generation, restored state, and clean GL errors. Instrumented texture readback, GPU echo, driver-source query, and source export counts after arm are all zero. Absence is scoped to instrumented paths, not a universal GL trace. These joins are activation evidence only; both records explicitly leave eligible/synthetic-hit invocation activity unproved.

Broad scene review likewise found no conspicuous lighting or tonal shift. Native-image inspection, rather than a scalar PSNR/tolerance gate, supports this bounded conclusion. No new P1/P2 still defect was demonstrated by these supplied artifacts.

## Limits and stopping boundary

CPU Iris temporal source ages are 54.787254 s candidate, 81.28381 s raw control, and 57.6591 s original. Clouds, entities, waving foliage, water, jitter, and histories are unsynchronized; screenshots are separate request/save observations. Exact per-pixel parity and attribution of small animated differences are therefore unearned. Tutorial/HUD/chat overlays are excluded from scene-quality judgement, and FPS text is not timing evidence.

Only one dry daytime coast camera is covered. There is no motion/popping/flicker, colored shadow/SSS stress scene, DH, PBR material pack, reflection correctness, reload/lifecycle, or other platform acceptance. Visible flower colors establish ordinary color cues only, not colored-shadow correctness. Actual eligible/raw/synth-hit activity is still unproved: uniform 1 and an unchanged still can coexist with no shortcut hits. This review does not demonstrate that work was avoided or accept optimization quality when the shortcut executes.

Terminal handback: five native crop artifacts, raw provenance verification, and this bounded still admission. Root owns the next practical observer-free cost decision and every runtime/build/resource action. No worker jobs remain running.

## Actual active work and denominator

Packed default settings enable AO, `AO_METHOD=0`, `AO_STRENGTH=1.00` and TAA.
The existing properties enable `world0/deferred` only when AO is enabled. Native
MEDIUM/HIGH/ULTRA have AO; MINIMUM/LOW disable it. Actual loaded choices must be
recorded rather than inferred from these defaults.

Packed producer line 87 calls the original four-direction/two-sample kernel with
radius 0.25. AO_METHOD 0 also reconstructs the normal using four depth reads;
thus a non-sky kernel has eight search-depth reads **plus four normal-depth reads**,
not just eight total depth reads. Original kernel logic, temporal dither evolution,
hand branch, AO method and strength are retained. Generated kernel changes only
depth fetches to explicit LOD0; the packed source confirms all affected depth
reads use it. Fallback fetches current depth and noise once before that kernel.

At 1920 × 1200, the intended producer viewport is 960 × 600: 576,000 producer
fragments versus 2,304,000 originally, or 75% fewer producer fragments. Geometry
coverage and sky early returns affect actual expensive invocation counts. The
consumer remains full resolution and resolves four RG texels for each non-sky
pixel; its discontinuity branch adds one current-pixel kernel. If geometry covers
the frame similarly and fallback fraction is `e`, approximate kernel count is
`0.25 + e` of native producer count. Above `e = 0.75`, it computes more complete
kernels than the native producer. This is an invocation estimate, not a total
time estimate: native resolve cost also changes and branch divergence/cache/ALU
costs are unknown.

Original native resolve reads four nearby depth values and four AO values with
depth weights; candidate replaces that with four combined AO/depth samples,
continuous confidence and optional unfiltered current-pixel AO. There is no
four-kernel fallback left in the actual r1c helper.

RT10 is RG32F, 8 bytes/texel, full allocation with only its lower-left quadrant
rendered. If Iris allocates the expected two ping-pong textures, additional storage
is 36,864,000 bytes (35.16 MiB) at 1920 × 1200. Existing native RT4/R8 stays allocated
for later cloud distance. Nominal producer output bytes are 4,608,000 versus
native R8's 2,304,000 per full viewport; four RG32F resolve fetches also carry more
AO data bytes than four R8 fetches. These are layout arithmetic, not measured
DRAM traffic; cache, clears and target behavior need runtime evidence.

For a producer-only saving estimate, eliminating 75% of producer time would
require that producer to represent at least 22.2% of original total frame time
to deliver 1.20× throughput (16.7% less frame time). That calculation ignores
changes to native resolve cost and new reconstruction/fallback/bandwidth; it is
not a bound on the actual combined candidate. No observed producer cost or +20%
result exists here.

## Concrete cost/quality risks

**Medium, source counterexample to silhouette-only fallback:**
`patches/experiments/bsl-real-budget-r1/reconstruct.glsl` lines 25–44 takes the
minimum depth confidence of all four taps and executes fallback for any result
below 1. A smooth sloping surface can meet that condition. For current positive
depth 10 blocks, tolerance is 0.25 blocks; a neighboring depth 10.10 gives relative
delta 0.4, smoothstep value 0.104 and confidence 0.896. That is a full kernel
invocation despite continuous geometry. Full confidence requires *every* sampled
depth difference to be at most 0.0625 blocks here (0.25 × tolerance). Farther than
25 blocks, the corresponding threshold is 0.25% of current depth. Thus "smooth
pixels execute zero fallback kernels" and "only discontinuity regions" are not
guaranteed by this predicate. This is direct substitution into packed arithmetic,
not a GPU reproduction. Grazing-angle ground/walls and dense foliage are decisive
cost scenes. A smooth confidence blend does not make execution cost gradual.

**Medium, visible-noise risk at silhouettes and motion:** helper lines 13–17
return one native current-pixel AO kernel raised to AO_STRENGTH. Native original
resolve instead depth-filters four full-resolution AO samples before applying
strength. At confidence zero, candidate deliberately removes that spatial filter;
native sample count alone does not establish native noise or temporal quality.
Near silhouettes, hand edges, contact shadows, thin leaves/fences and camera pans
can flicker or change darkness as half-grid samples/fallback mix change. This is
a reason for representative runtime inspection, not an observed artifact.

**Bounded compatibility defect, intentional pilot boundary:** both shared program
includes issue `#error` when the private flag is enabled outside Overworld, without
AO, or with DH/Voxy. Nether/End wrappers share them, so enabled dimension changes
are unsupported, not faithful safe behavior for a general adapter. No compile
guard requires TAA, so TAA-off configurations can enter the reduced path despite
unverified quality. Native AO_METHOD 1 remains in generated source but was not
covered by the recorded offline checks. This candidate must not be represented
as DH/PBR/all-options/multiversion support or promoted without a safe policy.

Odd sizes, resize, producer sampling phase and half-grid detail remain unverified.
For even sizes, producer UVs sample at half-grid centers while reconstruction
reads exact centers of the populated lower-left physical texture region; those
coordinates are consistent with the intended allocation/viewport mechanism.
They do not prove actual Iris scale/flip/sampler interpretation on the Mac.
